newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks track bond market gains.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks track bond market gains.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks rallied Tuesday as they took their cue from strength in bonds following more signs that the economy was slowing at a moderate pace.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 43.98 points at 6,016.71 after a morning of erratic fluctuations between 6,006.65 and 5,959.69.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on moderate volume of 254 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq Composite index was off 5.19 points at 1,210.70 amid renewed weakness in technology stocks. The American Stock Exchange index was up 0.08 at 566.63.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond soared more than 1-1/2 points, cutting its yield to 6.72 percent from 6.84 percent on Monday.

Financial markets were buoyed by a smaller than expected increase in the government's index of workers' compensation for the third quarter, which was up 0.6 percent after a 0.8 percent gain in the previous three months.
The overall increase in employee compensation costs in the third quarter -- the smallest in a year -- was below the 0.8 percent rise expected by Wall Street economists.

Also boosting sentiment was the consumer confidence index, which fell to 106.2 in October from a revised 111.8 in September. The figure was expected at 110.6, according to a Reuter survey of economists.
But the mood of traders was cautious as investors' focused on next week's elections.

"You have a situation in which the buyers are stepping away from the plate ahead of the election," said Scott Bleier, chief investment strategist at Prime Charter Ltd. "Buyers are planning to keep their powder dry until they see what happens to the market on election day (Nov. 5)," he said.
In addition to trepidation ahead of the elections, not to mention a full week of data climaxing with Friday's October jobs report, the market has become overbought, analysts said.
"Between July and mid-October, the S&P 500 was up 15 percent from its intraday lows," said Chris Callies, chief investment strategist at CS First Boston.
CompUSA was down 4-3/4 at 52-5/8 after Salomon Brothers said the stock could come under pressure due to worsening conditions in the computer retail industry.
International Business Machines Corp. was down 7/8 at 126-1/4, Compaq Computer Corp. lost 2-3/8 at 68-1/4, Hewlett-Packard Co. was down 7/8 at 44-3/8 and Tandy Corp. lost 3/4 at 39-1/4.
